chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Do not try the sharpness of your tongue against Him Who gave you the power to speak, nor the eloquence of your speaking against Him Who set you on the right path.

key_terms.أَنْطَقَكَ: He gave you the power to speak
key_terms.سَدَّدَكَ: He set you on the right path

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to direct the sharpness of one's tongue towards God?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of the 'sharp tongue' (dharab al-lisan) to warn against using the faculties granted by God to critique or complain about the Giver. This teaching underscores the Shia concept of *shukr* (gratitude) not merely as a feeling, but as the proper utilization of divine gifts in their intended direction, preventing the spiritual arrogance of challenging divine wisdom.
